blocks.text: To monitor health facility preparedness to perform signal functions
To monitor actual performance of signal functions
To monitor morbidities and mortality arising from gaps identified in the specific signal functions
To determine competences in EmONC among health care providers in the health facility

paragraphs: Facility level: (Level 2, Level 3a, Level 3b, Level 4, Level 5, Level 6)
Does this facility provide post abortion care services?
If yes for above, in which service area is the service provided? If no, proceed to the next question.
What is the total number of women who delivered at this facility across all three months preceding this assessment?
(Use the maternity register to count all women who delivered at the facility.)
Availability of MNH policy and guideline documents
Confirm physically if the documents listed below are available.
National Guidelines for Quality Obstetric and Perinatal Care (current edition)
about the last 24 hours; All shifts should be covered to score a ‘YES’ …
What is the total number of staff in the maternity and newborn units?
Have at least 2 skilled and trained birth attendants, who can currently perform routine delivery, been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can currently administer parenteral antibiotics, been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can currently administer uterotonics been avail- able at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can currently administer anticonvulsants been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can cur- rently perform manual removal of placenta been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can cur- rently perform manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can currently perform assisted vaginal delivery been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can currently perform new-born resuscitation with a bag and mask been available at all times?
Has an operating theatre team (Doctor, anesthetist, 2 theatre nurses) to perform caesarean section been available at all times? (All must be there to score)
Has at least 1 provider trained and can cur- rently process blood for transfusion avail- able at all times?
Has at least 1 provider trained and can cur- rently administer blood transfusion been available at all times?
Has at least 1 provider working in maternity unit trained on EmONC?
Has at least 1 provider with the knowledge of the use of NASG?

2. EQUIPMENT and SUPPLIES: Are the following currently in working order and available in quantity enough to satisfy the current caseload for one month in maternity? The questions do not refer to other departments.
Enough for current caseload for at least one
PPH Management kit (Large bore cannulas, Misoprostol, balloon tamponade, IV fluid, giving sets, 2-way Foleys catheters, and  specimen bottles)
Blood pressure measurement equipment (Digital BP machine or sphygmomanometer + stethoscope)
MVA kit (2 pairs of sterile gloves, 1 tray, 1 kidney dish, 1 gallipot, sponge holding forceps, ovum forceps, tenaculum, karmas cannula and adapter, syringe and piston,

Delivery Kit (5 Green towels, 1 Tray 10*14, 2 straight artery forceps 8’, cord scissors, episiotomy scissors, 2 needle holder 7 inches, 2 large kidney dish 10 inches, cord clamps, and 1 Gallipot) –Randomly check 1 kit for contents)
Ambu bag (200-300 ML capacity) with masks (neonatal – pre-term (size 0))
Ambu bag (200-300 ML capacity) with masks (neonatal – term (size 1))

2. EQUIPMENT and SUPPLIES: Are the fol- lowing currently in working order and available in quantity enough to satisfy the current caseload for one month in maternity? The questions do not refer to other departments.
Enough for current caseload for at least one
Ambu bag (1.5 L capacity) with masks (adult)
Fetoscope/handheld fetal heart monitor / digital fetoscope
Functional suction machines and catheters or penguin suction
Functional Infant Resuscitation Unit/ Radiant Warmer/Resuscitaire
Oxygen set (portable cylinder or central wall supply with Mask or nasal cannula with mask tubing and flow meter) or
Urine strips (both Proteinuria and sugar dip sticks) in the labor ward and laboratory.

2. EQUIPMENT and SUPPLIES: Are the following  currently in working order and available in quantity enough to satisfy the current caseload for one month in maternity? The questions do not refer to other departments.
Enough for current caseload for at least one
Is there a functioning refrigerator available for cold-chain drugs and lab reagents in the facility that is powered 24/7? (excludes KEPI fridges)
Complete C- section set (1 Mayo Scissors 14.5cm TC Straight; 1 Mayo Scissors 14.5cm TC Curved; 1x Mayo Hager Needle
Holder 16cm TC; 1 Heaney Needle Holder 21cm TC; 1 Scalpel Handle 4; 4 Blades for
Dissection Forceps 16cm; 1 Tissue Forceps 1:2 16cm; 1 Lane Forceps 1:2 18cm; 6 Kelly Forceps 14cm Straight 6 Kelly Forceps 14cm Curved; 2 Crile Forceps 1:2 14cm; 1
Is there any blood/blood products currently stored in the facility with blood giving sets/transfusion sets?
Blood grouping and cross-matching kit to include each of water bath, centrifuge, and reagents cold chain blood carriers
Is there a functioning refrigerator available in the facility that is powered 24/7 for storing blood?
In the most recent referral, did you notify or were you notified of a referral before the patient arrived in the receiving facility?
Does the maternity unit has access to functional phone?
Do you have access to ambulance services available 24/7 for maternity referrals to higher level facilities?
Was the most recent referral accompanied by a skilled health personnel?
3. DRUGS: Are the following drugs in stock and not expired?
Parenteral oxytocin (Only Score yes if cold chain is maintained)
3. DRUGS: Are the following drugs in stock and not expired?
Local Anesthetic agent for IM (e.g., lignocaine)
Anti-hypertensive  oral drugs (Methyldopa/ labetalol/ Nifedipine/ Hydralazine) Score yes if any is available)
Spinal anesthesia with assorted spinal needles
IV Fluids assorted (Normal saline or Ringer’s lactate or Half strength Darrow’s-HSD) with IV administration set
IV Fluids assorted (10% ,5% dextrose) with IV administration set
Is there running water in the maternity unit?
Has electricity been available 24/7 including a combination of back-up power (Solar, generator, rechargeable batteries etc) sources available?
Does the facility have disability friendly services, for example, sanitary facilities, adjustable beds, sign language, ramp?

Please select 5 labour care guide at random. Have the LCGs been appropriately used to monitor labour for ALL of the following: foetal heart rate, maternal condition and  reporting of the outcome of labour.
